references.text: Also describes the age of service for the Levites, but here from 25 years and upward, ending at 50 years. Shows variation in the age requirements for Levitical service.
Parallel text concerning the sons of Kohath with the same age requirement (30–50 years) for service in the tabernacle.
The same age requirement (30–50 years) applies to the service of the sons of Merari at the tent of meeting.
Repeats the age requirement of 30–50 years for those who were to serve at the tent of meeting.
Confirms the age limits of 30–50 years for the Levites' service in the tent of meeting.
Yet another confirmation of the age requirement of 30–50 years for service in the tent of meeting.
Summarizes that all men between 30 and 50 years old were mustered for service at the tent of meeting.
David changed the age limit for the Levites to 20 years, showing development in the rules for Levitical service.
Explains the change in the age requirement from 30 to 20 years for Levitical service under David.
Under Hezekiah, Levites from 20 years and upward were registered for service, showing continued development of the age requirements.
After the exile, Levites from 20 years old were appointed to oversee the work on the house of the Lord.
